children.text: About
4km

northeast of downtown Baguio, this lookout park gazes over Benguet's old gold and copper mining valleys and the Cordillera ridges. Pair it with the souvenir street, ube jam from the Good Shepherd Convent, The Mansion, and Wright Park for an easy half-day loop.
Mines View Park is a lookout park set at the tip of a ridge about
4km

northeast of downtown Baguio. A winding stone stairway beside the parking area leads down to an observation deck shaded by pines, with the deep valleys of Itogon and layer upon layer of ridges spread out below. The park takes its name from the view of Benguet Corporation's old gold and copper mines in this valley, and on clear days you can see as far as the Amburayan Valley.
The Benguet area was long the center of gold mining in the Philippines. After the Benguet Consolidated Mining Company, the forerunner of Benguet Corporation, was founded in
, gold was mined all over the Itogon valleys, and the Itogon mine has been officially inactive since
. The bare patches and zigzag roads you see on the slopes from the deck are traces of that era, and villages and vegetable plots have since filled in between them.

From the entrance down to the deck, souvenir shops and stalls line terraced steps, making this one of Baguio's main shopping streets too. They sell Cordillera textiles, carved bulul figures, Baguio brooms, strawberry jam, and peanut brittle, and photo spots where you put on a feathered headdress and pose with ponies or St. Bernard dogs are a local fixture. About
5–10 minutes
away on foot is the Good Shepherd Convent, famous for its ube jam.
The park is run by the City of Baguio and, according to the city tourism portal, is open
with an adult entrance fee of
. The deck alone takes just
30 minutes–1 hour
, but the Good Shepherd Convent, The Mansion, and Wright Park all lie within
2km
, so it is easy to string them into a half-day route. It suits families on their first trip to Baguio and travelers who want mountain scenery and souvenir shopping in a short time.

blocks.title: Looking down on the mining valley from the deck

children.text: From the railing of the deck below the stone steps, you look down into the Itogon valley. The old mine scars and zigzag roads on the slopes, and the villages along the ridges, all come into view at once. The view is clearest before
, before mist fills the valley.
The park opens at
, so you can watch light spread over the ridges around sunrise. On cool mornings in
November–February
you may find low clouds lying in the valley, and on clear days you can see as far as the ridges toward Mount Ugo.

The terraced shops running from the entrance to the deck sell Cordillera textiles, carved bulul figures, Baguio brooms, strawberry jam, and peanut brittle. Prices for the same item vary from shop to shop, so compare two or three and bargain politely.

blocks.title: Traditional costumes and St. Bernard photo spot

children.text: There are photo spots where you can rent a feathered headdress and traditional Igorot clothing or pose with St. Bernard dogs and ponies. The cost is usually a tip of around
, so confirm the price before taking photos.
Stalls sell snacks such as strawberry taho topped with strawberry syrup (about
), grilled corn, and banana cue. Around
December–April
, strawberry season, vendors also set out Benguet strawberries by the basket.

and can be visited free of charge Tuesday to Sunday,

The Good Shepherd Convent often sells out or closes early in the afternoon, so on the afternoon route it is safer to stop by separately the next morning. Other downtown sights are covered in the
Baguio
entry.
First, get to Baguio. Victory Liner, Joy Bus, and Solid North buses run almost 24 hours from Cubao, Pasay, and PITX in Manila, taking
4–6 hours
via TPLEX. Fares run about
one way depending on the class.
Bus and jeepney fares went up on
September 28, 2026
, so check the latest fares when booking. Tickets sell out fast on weekends, holidays, and during Panagbenga.
From Clark International Airport (CRK), direct buses to Baguio take about
3–4 hours
. Baguio's Loakan Airport has no scheduled passenger flights.
Take a jeepney marked "Mines View" from the loading area around Mabini Street below Session Road. The ride takes
15–20 minutes
and costs about
The last stop is near the Good Shepherd Convent, so you can visit the convent shop first and then walk to the park entrance. Routes and loading areas can change, so ask at your hotel first.
It is about
5km
from Burnham Park or Session Road,
10–15 minutes
without traffic, and the fare is about
. Always ask the driver to turn on the meter.
Taxis are hard to catch in front of the park on weekend afternoons, so use the queue at the taxi stand by the entrance or walk a little to the main road.
From Manila, driving up to Baguio via NLEX–SCTEX–TPLEX and Marcos Highway takes about
4–5 hours
. Kennon Road is often closed for rockfall and repairs, so check whether it is open first.
The park's parking lot holds about 50 cars and fills up by mid-morning on weekends and holidays. The city tourism portal lists no parking fee, but attendants sometimes ask for a small amount.
From the park entrance to the Good Shepherd Convent is a
5–10 minute
walk along Gibraltar Road, and shops line the way, so the walk never gets dull.
The Mansion and Wright Park are about
1.7km
away by road,
5–10 minutes
by taxi. Traffic is heavy and some stretches have narrow sidewalks, so with children or older travelers a taxi is easier than walking.
Mines View Park is all about the view, so weather and time of day decide how much you will enjoy it. Baguio is a highland city about
above sea level with an average annual temperature of about
, and in the
November–April
dry season the skies are clear enough to see distant ridges across the valley. In
December–February
, dawn temperatures drop to around
, so the morning wind on the deck is quite cold.
The city's biggest event, the Panagbenga Flower Festival, ran from
February 1
to
March 8
in
, and the deck is busiest during the festival, the
March–May
peak season, Holy Week, and the year-end holidays. In the
June–October

rainy season, mist and showers roll in most afternoons and often white out the valley, so go early in the morning. When a typhoon passes, mountain roads carry a landslide risk, so it is safer to postpone your visit.

Quiet inns and guesthouses are scattered through the pine woods along Gibraltar Road and Outlook Drive around the park, a convenient choice if you want to walk to the deck early in the morning. If you also want easy access to the market, restaurants, and bus terminals, downtown hotels around Session Road and Burnham Park are better, and the park is
10–15 minutes
away by taxi. Guesthouses run about
a night and mid-range hotels about
; rates rise sharply during Panagbenga and Holy Week, so book early.

Inside the park you can eat street snacks such as strawberry taho, grilled corn, and banana cue, but there are few proper restaurants. The ube jam, strawberry jam, peanut brittle, and cookies from the Good Shepherd Convent shop are Baguio's signature gifts, while the same kinds of jam, brooms, and woodcarvings are generally cheaper at the public market. For meals, head to restaurants at Camp John Hay,
10–15 minutes
away by car, or the long-standing bakeries and cafes on Session Road; on cold evenings, a hot soup like bulalo (beef bone marrow soup) hits the spot.
Arriving before
lets you avoid both the tour buses and the mist. It is most crowded from
Many places, including the entrance and the stalls, take cash only, so bring plenty of small bills such as
, and
Go to the Good Shepherd Convent in the morning to get the popular jams. There is a per-person purchase limit, and lines form in peak season.
The Mansion is closed on Mondays, so to cover Mines View, Good Shepherd, The Mansion, and Wright Park in one go, plan for Tuesday to Sunday.
Compare two or three shops and bargain for souvenirs, but if you want the same items for less, go to the public market.
The wind on the deck is cold even in the daytime, so bring a light jacket, and wear shoes with firm soles so you don't slip on wet stone steps.
The deck itself only needs
30 minutes–1 hour
, so spend the rest of your time at the Good Shepherd Convent or walking in Wright Park.
If you don't want photo services or pony rides, a polite no is enough. If you do use them, agree on the price and duration first.
Some restrooms around the park charge a fee, so it helps to carry coins and tissues.

On weekends, holidays, during Panagbenga, Holy Week, and the year-end holidays, the deck stairs and access road get extremely crowded and the road in front of the park jams up. At these times, arrive before
or move your visit to a weekday.
Do not step beyond the railing or toward the cliff edge. In
, ground cracks were reported inside the park and the city council called for a geohazard study. Follow barrier lines and construction screens, and check the latest notices.
Pickpockets may operate on the crowded stairs and souvenir street, so keep your phone and wallet in a bag worn in front.
It is best not to use the animal photo spots or pony rides if the animals look exhausted or are being handled roughly.
In the rainy season, thick mist and showers can leave almost no view, and after typhoons, landslides sometimes block mountain roads. Check the forecast and road conditions before you set out.
The City of Baguio is considering charging tourists an environmental user's fee, aiming to introduce it in
. Entrance fees and other charges may change, so check the latest notices.
